verdicts.decision_note: The client establishes the $5 commission behavior that routes no-referral primary-mint commissions to a random existing NFT holder.
The client identifies a material unresolved recipient edge case for mint #1, when no existing NFT holder is available.
The client expands the executable payout condition so an invalid referral code uses the same random-holder commission allocation as no code.
First target-specific implementation claim describing founder routing for mint #1 and random existing-holder routing for later no-referral mints.
First concrete runtime failure showing that a completed no-referral mint did not award its commission to a random holder.
The client explicitly rejects founder-default payout routing and requires no-referral commissions to be distributed randomly among existing holders.
Target-specific post-failure implementation claim that no-referral mints now generate a randomly allocated commission.
The source concerns registration of random commissions in aggregate accounting, which belongs to Commission Accounting Accuracy rather than recipient allocation.
The client establishes the executable rule that each completed no-referral primary mint issues one $5 commission.

value_updates.allocation_condition: A primary mint after mint #1 is completed with no referral code or an invalid referral code.
value_updates.commission_issuance_rate: One randomly allocated $5 commission per completed no-referral primary mint after mint #1.

verdicts.decision_note: The accepted first-mint exception changes payout eligibility; the edit narrows the prior all-mints allocation condition so it does not conflict with that exception.
The client unambiguously accepts the implementation rule that processRandomReferral credits the randomly selected token with the $5 commission.

missing_event_candidates.description: The requirement that randomly issued commissions register in commission totals is misrouted and should be checked against the Commission Accounting Accuracy lifecycle.
